Standard Human

From the first tools chipped from stone to the sprawling cities that touch the clouds, Standard Humans have thrived by bending without breaking. They are masters of adaptation, taking what exists and reshaping it to meet the needs of the moment. Their history is one of migration, invention, and reinvention — a constant cycle of trial and error that has forged a race capable of surviving almost anywhere. In times of peace, they build; in times of strife, they endure. They are neither the strongest nor the swiftest, neither the most cunning nor the most enduring — yet they find ways to close the gap through sheer persistence and ingenuity. Their cultures are as varied as the landscapes they inhabit, from tightly-knit village communities to sprawling multicultural metropolises. Outsiders often underestimate them because of their lack of extremes, but this very balance allows them to blend into nearly any environment. To meet a Human is to meet a puzzle of influences — traits borrowed, adapted, and made their own over generations. They excel in cooperation, forging alliances with other peoples, and in competition, driving themselves to match and surpass their peers. For all their accomplishments, they carry a restlessness that pushes them toward new horizons, sometimes at the cost of appreciating what they already have.

Educated Human

In every era, Educated Humans have chosen the pursuit of knowledge as their path through life. Their legacy is one of meticulous study, where each generation stands on the shoulders of the last, adding to the collective memory preserved in books, archives, and now digital vaults. These are the record-keepers, the archivists, and the planners whose efforts have shaped civilizations as much as the warriors and builders. Raised in environments where learning is not just encouraged but expected, they hone their minds in lecture halls, laboratories, and debate chambers. Their communities often revolve around centers of knowledge — universities, research guilds, or think tanks — where ideas are tested, debated, and refined. They tend toward patience, preferring the slow certainty of proven methods over the gamble of improvisation. Outsiders may see them as overcautious or even aloof, but to them, careful thought is the surest path to lasting solutions. Many Educated Humans specialize so deeply in their chosen field that they risk becoming disconnected from everyday life, yet their insights can solve problems no one else could even define. They bring order to chaos through analysis, though they may falter when that chaos refuses to fit the models they know. Their presence in a community often ensures stability, foresight, and the preservation of culture for generations to come.

Nomadic Human

Nomadic Humans are wanderers by tradition, their histories written in the dust of countless roads and the logs of caravans that crossed the world’s widest reaches. Their origin lies in the meeting places between civilizations, where trade, travel, and adaptation are matters of survival. Over generations, they have mastered the art of living light — carrying only what they can repair, barter, or trade along the way. They know the routes that bind distant lands together and the hidden ways known only to those who walk them. Their culture prizes self-reliance, but also recognizes that survival on the road depends on mutual aid; a stranger one day may be a savior the next. They are storytellers and deal-makers, carrying news, goods, and ideas from one corner of the world to another. While others build walls, they map the ways around them. Their adaptability makes them skilled mediators between cultures, though some see them as rootless and unreliable. In truth, their loyalty is to the road itself and the people who travel it with them. Meeting a Nomadic Human is to meet someone shaped by the horizon — alert to opportunity, wary of traps, and always ready to move when the winds change. They are both the lifeblood of commerce and the keepers of paths others have forgotten.

Hill Dwarf

Hill Dwarves are the enduring craftsmen of the lowlands, where rolling hills meet exposed stone and deep quarries. Their legacy is written in bridges that have stood for centuries and hearths that have warmed a hundred winters. Unlike their mountain kin who retreat into lofty citadels, Hill Dwarves keep their settlements open to travelers, valuing trade and neighborly bonds as much as stone and mortar. Generations of quarrying, masonry, and brewing have honed their bodies into sturdy frames built for hard work and long days. They are slow to anger but slower to forgive, and their loyalty must be earned with consistent action. Pride in craft is their greatest virtue and their greatest flaw — a Hill Dwarf will labor months longer than needed if it means the work will last another lifetime. Outsiders often find them blunt to the point of rudeness, but behind their words is a commitment to honesty that borders on sacred. They are known for their barrel-aged spirits, meticulous engineering, and buildings that seem to grow stronger with age. Quick fixes and shoddy work earn nothing but contempt from them. In a world that changes quickly, they are an anchor, building not for the moment, but for the generations yet to come.

Mountain Dwarf

Mountain Dwarves are born to the heights, where air is thin, snow falls like shards, and the earth itself shifts underfoot. Their cities cling to cliffsides and perch above yawning valleys, held in place by rope bridges, anchor bolts, and sheer will. Centuries of living in constant danger from avalanches, rockslides, and storms have shaped them into master riggers and structural engineers. Every step is measured, every knot inspected, and every handhold tested before weight is placed upon it. Precision and preparation are cultural laws, and neglecting them is the highest form of recklessness. Their climbing harnesses and rigging systems are as much a part of their identity as their beards. Mountain Dwarves are not given to boasting until the work is done, but when they do, it is with the satisfaction of those who have defied nature and won. Outsiders often marvel at their feats, yet fail to grasp the quiet discipline that underlies every success. They can be slow to trust outsiders with dangerous work, preferring to see proof of skill before handing over a rope. To live among them is to live in constant awareness of the risks — and the thrill — of life at the edge. They have carried their craft into the modern age, turning their talents to building and maintaining structures that scrape the sky or pierce the crust of alien worlds.

Deep Dwarf

Deep Dwarves are the underworld’s cartographers, navigating a labyrinth of stone and darkness few on the surface can imagine. Their earliest halls were carved in pursuit of ore and water, and over the centuries they transformed tunnels into sprawling subterranean cities. They know the sound of stone shifting in its sleep, the subtle vibrations of a distant collapse, and the perfect spot to place a support that will hold for a hundred years. Communication in the deep is often wordless — a code of taps, knocks, and vibrations that carry farther than voices. Silence is safety; noise is danger. Deep Dwarves value precision in all things, for a single misjudged blast or misplaced beam can spell disaster for an entire settlement. Outsiders often find their manner quiet and distant, but this is the reserve of those who live where one wrong move can bury a thousand lives. They have little patience for surface dwellers who underestimate the weight of stone or the value of caution. Their skill in navigating and securing tunnels makes them invaluable in times of crisis, whether clearing a collapse or reinforcing a crumbling foundation. Though they rarely seek the open sky, they will endure it for work that serves the clan or secures vital resources. To earn their trust is to be given safe passage through the world’s most dangerous depths.

Forge Dwarf

Forge Dwarves are the industrial heartbeats of dwarvenkind, carrying the legacy of the anvil into the age of roaring furnaces and precision machining. Their ancestors once worked the deep forges beneath mountains, but over centuries they migrated into bustling cities where smoke stacks replaced stalactites. In their hands, ancient techniques blend seamlessly with modern tools; the clang of a hammer on steel harmonizes with the whir of lathes and the sizzle of welding arcs. They are perfectionists by nature, refusing to release a piece of work until it meets standards measured in microns. Their bodies are built for endurance, with thick arms and chests conditioned to endure long hours in sweltering heat. Forge Dwarves take pride in their ability to adapt their craft to any metal, from wrought iron to star-forged alloys, yet they hold fast to the belief that every project is a reflection of its maker’s honor. Outsiders find them intense, sometimes to the point of intimidation, but beneath the soot and gruff tone is a deep camaraderie for those who share their work ethic. Their guild halls are equal parts workshop, training ground, and family hearth, where apprentices learn both the craft and the discipline to wield it responsibly. In their eyes, a shoddy product is a stain not only on the maker but on the entire forge line. They see themselves as the keepers of quality in a world increasingly willing to cut corners, and they wear that responsibility like armor.

Gnome

Gnomes are the miniature titans of precision engineering, blending an almost obsessive curiosity with the fine motor skills of a master jeweler. Their history is rooted in artisan workshops and hidden warrens where gears and springs clicked long before the rise of modern technology. Over the centuries, they became innovators in delicate machinery, intricate clockworks, and, more recently, microcircuitry and robotics. Gnomes are rarely content with a working device — they must see if it can be made smaller, faster, or more efficient. Their minds race ahead of the present, dreaming of new designs even as they tweak the last. They are fiercely loyal to their guilds, which act as both professional networks and extended families, ensuring every creation meets strict standards. While quick to share ideas, they are protective of their best designs, guarding them with both secrecy and clever failsafes. Their small stature belies a large presence in technological advancement, with their innovations often sparking revolutions in multiple fields. Outsiders may find them eccentric, sometimes maddeningly so, but their oddities are often the byproduct of a mind juggling a dozen projects at once. A Gnome’s workshop is a chaotic wonderland of half-finished devices, blueprints pinned to every surface, and a constant background hum of whirring parts. They view their work as both craft and legacy, knowing that a single brilliant invention can change the course of history.

Tinker Gnomes are the restless innovators of the gnomish world, driven less by perfection and more by the thrill of creation. Their history is marked by bursts of progress — wild, unpredictable leaps in technology spurred by late-night experiments and half-mad inspiration. They are quick with their hands and quicker with ideas, often producing gadgets before anyone can decide if they’re needed. Failure is not a deterrent; it is an expected and even celebrated part of their process. Their workshops are cluttered with prototypes, some brilliant, others dangerous, many both. Tinker Gnomes have a knack for spotting unconventional solutions, turning scrap into lifesaving tools or devastating weapons with equal ease. They are natural problem-solvers, but their solutions sometimes bring as many complications as they resolve. While they share the gnomish love for fine engineering, their work favors speed and improvisation over polish and durability. This makes them invaluable in emergencies, when a working tool right now matters more than one that will last a lifetime. Outsiders often underestimate them due to their size or whimsical demeanor, but few doubt their genius after seeing them work under pressure. They are storytellers through their machines, each invention a reflection of their boundless curiosity and refusal to accept “impossible” as an answer. In a world of constant change, Tinker Gnomes thrive, always chasing the next great idea.

Trickwire Gnomes are masters of caution and calculation, blending the skills of traditional trapmakers with the cunning of modern infiltration experts. Their origins lie in the hidden warrens of fortified gnome enclaves, where securing perimeters was a matter of survival and ingenuity. Over centuries, they adapted these skills to the emerging frontiers of information warfare, treating every lock and every line of code as puzzles to be solved. They see danger as an equation—one that can always be anticipated, mitigated, or redirected. Their sharp minds and steady hands make them equally comfortable crafting delicate clockwork snares or dissecting encrypted data streams. Trickwire Gnomes rarely rush into a space without first mapping its vulnerabilities, and they leave behind security measures that are both functional and artful. Though they prize foresight over brute force, their methods are not without risk; one misread pattern can turn preparation into liability. In their own communities, they are valued as protectors, analysts, and strategic advisors. Outsiders often find them reserved, even paranoid, but those who earn their trust find an ally whose preparations can mean the difference between victory and disaster. Their legacy is one of vigilance—an unending watch over the borders, whether those are physical gates or the invisible edges of a network.

Standard Human

From the first tools chipped from stone to the sprawling cities that touch the clouds, Standard Humans have thrived by bending without breaking. They are masters of adaptation, taking what exists and reshaping it to meet the needs of the moment. Their history is one of migration, invention, and reinvention — a constant cycle of trial and error that has forged a race capable of surviving almost anywhere. In times of peace, they build; in times of strife, they endure. They are neither the strongest nor the swiftest, neither the most cunning nor the most enduring — yet they find ways to close the gap through sheer persistence and ingenuity. Their cultures are as varied as the landscapes they inhabit, from tightly-knit village communities to sprawling multicultural metropolises. Outsiders often underestimate them because of their lack of extremes, but this very balance allows them to blend into nearly any environment. To meet a Human is to meet a puzzle of influences — traits borrowed, adapted, and made their own over generations. They excel in cooperation, forging alliances with other peoples, and in competition, driving themselves to match and surpass their peers. For all their accomplishments, they carry a restlessness that pushes them toward new horizons, sometimes at the cost of appreciating what they already have.

Every step is measured, every knot inspected, and every handhold tested before weight is placed upon it. Precision and preparation are cultural laws, and neglecting them is the highest form of recklessness. Outsiders often marvel at their feats, yet fail to grasp the quiet discipline that underlies every success.
